LESSON: MONEY

Grade: PP1
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: MEASUREMENT
Topic 3.5: Money

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Money. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. save money (coins and notes) 10 lessons (coins and notes) e) appreciate the use of Kenyan currency (coins and notes) in their daily life devices playing buying and selling.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. save money (coins and notes) 10 lessons (coins and notes) e) appreciate the use of Kenyan currency (coins and notes) in their daily life devices playing buying and selling.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to save money (coins and notes) 10 lessons (coins and notes) e) appreciate the use of Kenyan currency (coins and notes) in their daily life devices playing buying and selling. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Money.
2. Explain Money to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Money.
4. Show that you can: save money (coins and notes) 10 lessons (coins and notes) e) appreciate the use of Kenyan currency (coins and notes) in their daily life devices playing buying and selling.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Money. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Money important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. save money (coins and notes) 10 lessons (coins and notes) e) appreciate the use of Kenyan currency (coins and notes) in their daily life devices playing buying and selling.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
